investigations.name: colonies
investigations.title: Colony & Microfluidic Phenotype Quantification
investigations.description:
A phenotype-quantification investigation: measure emergent colony/microfluidic
phenotypes of whole-cell E. coli across a cost/fidelity ladder of cell models
and device geometries, using one shared phenotype panel (growth rate,
size-at-division, added length, inter-division time). It is organised as an
enabling compute foundation (Part A) that makes the science (Part B) runnable.

## Part A — Compute foundation (enabling infrastructure)

The colony composite wires N whole-cell agents (each embedding the 55-process
EcoliWCM via the bridge) into one pymunk 2D environment. Part A made it
single-machine-correct and cost-characterised:

- Daughter hydration through the engine + natural division 1->2->4 (after
  fixing mother-removal over-counting and daughter placement), coherent physics
  (jitter 0.5 -> 1e-4, coherent mass). [colonies-01, colonies-02; colony GIF]
- Per-cell wall is flat (~57 ms/tick/cell across N=1..8 on the 2026-07-26
  remote re-run @ f69f9690; pymunk is essentially free); the inner EcoliWCM is
  the whole cost, and the GIL is the single-process compute ceiling. The Ray
  protocol runs cells in separate OS processes and lifts that ceiling (~3.5x at
  N=16). [colonies-01, colonies-02]

Memory — the correction. Earlier framing (colonies-02/03) called the colony
"RAM-blocked by an unbounded native leak" and retracted the cells-per-node
budget. A focused per-process + tracemalloc hunt (2026-07-26) localized the
growth to the inner WCM's polypeptide-elongation step (82%) and mass-listener
(17%), and showed it is NOT an unbounded leak:
  - the truly-retained part is small (~0.2 MB/tick), the scipy LSODA
    integrator's rwork/iwork held per solve (equilibrium / two-component /
    charging ODEs);
  - the rest — the scary ~1.4 MB/tick on the dev mini — is allocator ARENA
    RETENTION from the elongation step's large per-tick numpy working arrays:
    freed, but macOS doesn't return the pages, so RSS climbs (invisible to
    tracemalloc). On glibc / Linux — the HPC target — the growth collapses:
    the REAL 55-process colony, built for glibc in a Linux container, grew RSS
    0.225 MB/tick vs ~1.6 on the macOS mini (7x less; end-to-end validated), and
    a synthetic reproduction of just the arena churn grew 0.017 MB/tick (0.000
    with periodic malloc_trim(0)) — so the arena-churn component is fully
    reclaimed on Linux and the residual 0.225 is the real scipy-LSODA retention.
So the "leak" was substantially a macOS measurement artifact. On the HPC
(Linux) target the colony's memory is bounded (arena churn reclaimed by glibc +
optional malloc_trim; residual ~0.2 MB/tick scipy retention is a small, named
optimization target). The compute foundation is HPC-deployable; memory is a
characterised limitation, not the story. [colonies-03; leak hunt 2026-07-26]

## Part B — Phenotype quantification (the science)

Part B reuses Part A's device geometries (mother machine, daughter machine,
free colony) and runs them across three cell-model tiers — a cheap simple
viva-munk agent, a growth-only surrogate, and the full EcoliWCM — all measured
through one shared phenotype panel. colonies-04 stands up the shared factory,
geometry builders, and phenotype extractor and validates it with simple agents.
colonies-05/06 run the two canonical viva-munk devices with simple agents
(running animation + size-at-division / birth->division-time / added-size
distributions; conclusions held for experimental data). colonies-08/09 run the
full whole-cell tier inside the device geometries. The surrogate tier and real
mother-machine-data comparison are planned follow-ons. Because the colony now
streams a bounded per-cell phenotype panel to zarr (ColonyPhenotypeRecorder),
the WCM-tier runs are length-bounded on the dev mini but unbounded on HPC.
investigations.question:
Do the emergent single-cell phenotypes of the whole-cell E. coli model —
adder size-homeostasis, the inter-division-time distribution, and the growth
rate — survive embedding into a physically-packed, dividing microcolony, and
do they match microfluidic-device data, across a cost/fidelity ladder of cell
models (simple viva-munk agent -> growth surrogate -> full 55-process WCM) run
in the canonical devices (mother machine, daughter machine, free colony)?
investigations.hypothesis:
Single-cell phenotype is a property of the cell model, not the container: the
WCM's adder size-homeostasis, inter-division-time CV, and growth rate are
preserved when cells are embedded in a pymunk 2D colony that grows, packs, and
divides, and they are reproduced (to tier-appropriate fidelity) by the cheaper
simple-agent and growth-surrogate tiers. The compute foundation needed to run
this — daughter hydration through the engine, natural division, coherent
physics, and bounded memory — is infrastructure, not the result.

investigations.name: multiscale-complexity-showcase
investigations.title: Multiscale Complexity in a Whole-Cell E. coli
investigations.question:
What emergent biological phenomena does v2ecoli produce that are invisible at any
single scale, and appear only when molecular, cellular, and population scales are
coupled? Where the model diverges from cited biology, what is the smallest principled
correction that closes the gap — and, just as importantly, can a disciplined loop tell
apart the three fates of a candidate defect: already-correct, structurally-limited, and
fixable? The investigation's real object is not any single number but the epistemics of
correcting a whole-cell model without fooling yourself.
investigations.hypothesis:
The whole-cell model expresses genuine multiscale complexity in three distinct
flavors: (1) cross-scale CONTROL — a single molecular signal (ppGpp) coordinates
ribosome allocation, replication initiation, and growth across scales; (2) nonlinear
FLUX REALLOCATION — central-carbon metabolism reroutes under stress with emergent
energetic consequences; (3) ORDER FROM NOISE — stochastic molecular events produce
statistically lawful single-cell and population heterogeneity. The disciplined
gap->fix->validate loop will, across these arcs, correctly sort each divergence into
already-correct, structural, or fixable, refuse an unprincipled fix, and — where a fix
is warranted — land it with a held-out check.

investigations.name: v2ecoli-baseline-showcase
investigations.title: v2ecoli Baseline Showcase: from ecoli-sources to a calibrated whole cell
investigations.question:
Can v2ecoli, starting from the raw ecoli-sources flat files, rebuild the
ParCa in full, run a wild-type baseline single-cell→division ensemble that
reproduces measured E. coli properties (doubling time, mass fractions, FBA
fluxes, proteome), and then characterize a perturbation response? This is a
demonstration walkthrough of the v2ecoli pipeline
(ecoli-sources → ParCa → calibrated whole cell → perturbation), not a test of
a scientific hypothesis. It also hands reviewers an explicit
perturbation-choice decision.

investigations.name: v2ecoli-pdmp
investigations.title: v2ecoli → PDMP Whole-Cell Model Reformulation
investigations.question:
Can v2ecoli's hybrid algorithmic whole-cell model be incrementally
transformed into a piecewise-deterministic Markov process (PDMP)
suitable for likelihood-based inference and causal discovery, without
discarding the biological knowledge encoded in the current WCM, and
while maintaining viable E. coli growth at every phase boundary?
investigations.hypothesis:
A six-phase incremental replacement — (0) Markov-blanket
characterization, (1) v2ecoli's multi-objective FBA → kinetic ODE
metabolism, (2) discrete-time → continuous-time jump processes,
(3) observation-likelihood and
Bayesian-interface infrastructure, (4) compiled column-centric runtime,
(5) Bayesian gene-function annotation — yields a PDMP-class WCM that
(a) reproduces Phase-0 interface statistics within tolerance at every
later phase, (b) admits well-formed process likelihoods at Phase 3,
(c) achieves ≥10³ parallel single-cell trajectories with near-zero
marshalling overhead at Phase 4, and (d) recovers known E. coli gene
functions with credible intervals on a benchmark set at Phase 5.
